headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.64 (95% CI: 0.43–0.95), suggesting that legumes is associated with a lower risk of bladder cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 77.91%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

studies.Title: Mediterranean Diet and Bladder Cancer Risk in Italy.
studies.Authors: Bravi F, Spei ME, Polesel J, Di Maso M, Montella M, Ferraroni M, Serraino D, Libra M, Negri E, La Vecchia C, Turati F
studies.Population: Hospital-based patients in Milan, Pordenone, Naples, and Catania

sample_size.excerpt: Distribution of 690 cases of bladder cancer and 665 controls according to age, sex, education, and other selected variables.
sample_size.location: Abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 690 + 665 = 1355

cases.excerpt: Cases consisted of 690 patients (595 men and 95 women) with incident diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma of the bladder and without previous history of other neoplasms (age range: 25–84 years, median: 67 years,), recruited in major general hospitals.

effect_size.excerpt: low consumption of the individual components of the MDS, we observed significant inverse associations for the intake of legumes (OR = 0.52, 95% CI, 0.40–0.69), vegetables (OR = 0.70, 95% CI, 0.53–0.92) and fish (OR = 0.68, 95% CI, 0.53–0.87); this is shown in supplementary Table S1 .

confidence_interval.excerpt: low consumption of the individual components of the MDS, we observed significant inverse associations for the intake of legumes (OR = 0.52, 95% CI, 0.40–0.69), vegetables (OR = 0.70, 95% CI, 0.53–0.92) and fish (OR = 0.68, 95% CI, 0.53–0.87); this is shown in supplementary Table S1 .

comparison.excerpt: When considering high vs. low consumption of the individual components of the MDS, we observed significant inverse associations for the intake of legumes

design.excerpt: The present analyses are based on a hospital-based case–control study carried out in four Italian areas—Milan, Pordenone, Naples, and Catania—in 2003–2014

timing.excerpt: Specifically, dietary habits in the two years preceding diagnosis for cases or interview for controls was evaluated using a valid and reproducible food frequency questionnaire (FFQ)

continent.excerpt: The present analyses are based on a hospital-based case–control study carried out in four Italian areas

ethnicity.excerpt: In our study, which was carried out on an Italian population, the higher adherence to the Mediterranean diet was related to a lower risk of bladder cancer.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: dietary habits in the two years preceding diagnosis for cases or interview for controls was evaluated using a valid and reproducible food frequency questionnaire (FFQ), including 80 foods and recipes as well as different types of alcoholic beverages

gender.excerpt: Results were similar in strata of sex
